parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime couples a hostile national layer with a comparatively protective state/province. Universal national exposures are documented: passports must now record birth-assigned sex, X markers are eliminated for new issues, travellers report confiscations and stranding, and a 2025 cable directs officers to refuse cases with document/sex discrepancies and consider lifetime fraud findings — an inescapable, every-crossing exposure for any trans visitor. However, there is no criminalisation of gender expression, a national hate-crime statute covers gender identity, and courts actively contest and enjoin several measures. This division itself sits in the national assessment's Low-Risk group: no bathroom ban (the Governor vetoed such bills), employment/public-accommodation protections, an adult-care access order, and only youth-focused restrictions judged unlikely to extend to adults. Pride's dissolution signals softening climate but is friction, not exposure. On-site, severity stays low; the operative hazard is the national border/document regime.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports must show birth-assigned sex; X markers ended; travellers report confiscation/stranding; 2025 cable instructs refusal on document-sex discrepancy and possible lifetime fraud bar. Universal, every-crossing exposure.
entry_documents.protection: None for the national layer; litigation pending. Existing X passports valid until expiry.
entry_documents.interaction: Border exposure follows the visitor into the state; state protections do not touch federal screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented for this division. National record documents conversion-model prison policies, forced labour and sexual abuse in immigration custody — remote but severe if custody occurs.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest here flows into national custody systems with the documented harms.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented for this division; national funding-based facility restrictions (single-sex per birth) affect federally funded spaces.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Governor vetoed bathroom and pronoun bills; state is not on the mapped ban lists; trespass-bathroom offence exists in other divisions, not here.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National sex-definition order can reach federally funded facilities despite state restraint.

care_services.exposure: For a travelling minor: state ban on surgery for trans minors since 2023; national rule proposals to bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 care.
care_services.protection: 2023 executive order grants state employees over 21 full gender-affirming coverage; adult visitors face no documented state care restriction.
care_services.interaction: Adult care access protected; minor's care access restricted — relevant to adult travelling with a trans minor.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National 'gender ideology' framing, counterterrorism language targeting 'radically pro-transgender' groups, and 'chemical/surgical mutilation' rhetoric raise hostility climate; education hotlines and the 2026 Pride dissolution show chilling locally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Courts and the civil-liberties union actively contest national measures; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetoric raises social and official hostility probability; no documented local enforcement against adults here.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces the state surgery ban and proposed national insurance bar; teacher-prosecution order chilling school support; hospital-records subpoenas; hotline for reporting schools.
minors_guardians.protection: Parent-veto restraint, 2019 family-court ruling, low-risk national classification; measures largely youth-targeted, courts contesting national layer.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian retains care responsibility but cannot obtain restricted services locally.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented for this division. National hate-crime data on sexual-orientation bias is secondary; trans panic defence remains available under common law.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; municipal ordinances in nine cities; state employment protections functioning.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists but is patchy; no division-specific violence record.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: which documents are believed at entry, enforcement of the fraud cable, unresolved Medicaid/Birth-certificate litigation interactions, stability of executive-order protections.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, legal-aid FAQ trackers, equality maps; state in documented Low-Risk group with adult-targeting judged unlikely.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are real but political-fragile; unknowns are open questions, not exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A features routine, unappealable exclusion of trans visitors at entry. Here entry screening is discretionary and litigated, no refusal pattern against this state's visitors is documented, and the division itself is protective — materially above 0.35-A.

0.55-B's extended secondary screening and discretionary refusal resemble the national passport/cable regime, which is this case's heaviest exposure. But this division adds documented nondiscrimination law, no facility ban, and adult care access, placing it above 0.55-B.

0.75-C shows trained officers, brief detention ending in release, and working appeal remedies. On the ground in this division the experience is comparable or better (no bathroom ban, protections operating); the national passport regime holds it at or slightly below 0.75-C, giving ~0.70.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences two regimes simultaneously. Locally: restrained, protective — no facility ban, vetoed bathroom bills, functioning anti-discrimination machinery, adult gender-affirming care access, and placement in the national Low-Risk group. Nationally: universal document exposure — birth-assigned-sex passports, ended X markers, discrepancy-based refusal and possible lifetime fraud findings — plus a hostile rhetoric layer and documented custody harms that are remote for an ordinary visitor. Courts are contesting the national layer, but it is operative now. Severity if outed locally is low; severity at the border is moderate-to-major (stranding, refusal, fraud bar) but not custodial or lethal. Minors add the state surgery ban and proposed insurance bar. Net: Reduced-to-Low Risk, ~0.70 — above the parent national average because the division's protective layer governs on-the-ground life, held below 0.75+ because the border regime reaches every visitor every crossing and is unresolved in court.
